summary: TS streaming: resume cookie sanitizer alters idempotency salt leading to duplicated tool/function executions on reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external webhook invocations and doubled tool/function executions after a client reconnects to a streaming session.

Impact:
- Reproduced against customer production traffic: duplicate side-effects (webhook posts) observed for ~2% of reconnect events during a multi-hour batch ingestion.
- Cause customer-visible inconsistencies and out-of-band downstream work (duplicate DB writes, duplicate notifications).

Environment:
- TS SDK (v1.8.3) streaming client behind an enterprise edge (cookie sanitizer) + Redwood hosted API in us-east.
- Dedicated enterprise account (NimbusHealth).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start a long-running streaming chat that requests several external tool calls (webhook-style) from the model.
2) Client loses connection and the browser-based frontend reconnects automatically using the SDK resume API; the resume token is stored in a cookie by the edge.
3) Edge sanitizer (corporate WAF) rewrites cookie characters: replaces '+' with '-', removes trailing '=' padding.
4) SDK resumes with the rewritten resume token.
5) Server treats the token as a different resume salt value and replays the pending tool calls instead of deduplicating them.

Expected behavior:
- Resume token canonicalization should preserve idempotency salt semantics across proxies and cookie sanitizers, or the server should normalize equivalent encodings so reconnects are idempotent.

Observed behavior:
- Resume token mangling by intermediate cookie sanitizer changes the idempotency salt; server treats resume as a fresh session in some code paths and re-executes pending tool calls, causing duplicate external side-effects.

Logs / snippets attached:
- Customer included webhook timestamps showing two closely spaced invocations.
- Server trace (sample): resume_token received (base64url-no-pad) => downstream resume hashing returns different nonce hash.

Customer impact & priority rationale:
- Enterprise customer with high downstream sensitivity to duplicates (billing/notifications).
- P1/Sev1 due to production impact and ability to trigger duplicates at scale.

investigation: Observed raw resume tokens from customer: 'Y29udGVudC50b2tlbi1iYXNlNjQ' (no padding) and server expected 'Y29udGVudC50b2tlbi1iYXNlNjQ='; decode path diverged leading to different nonce salt.
Confirmed WAF behavior: replacement of '+' -> '-' and stripping '=' padding for cookie compatibility (common in corporate proxies).
Reproduced locally by sending both canonical encodings; server routing logic used token raw string for idempotency salt before fix (string != canonicalized form).
Instrumented resume path: hashed_resume_salt = hash(raw_token) used downstream; when token encoding changed, hash changed => server replayed pending tool calls via 'resume as new' flow.
Temporary mitigation validated: server-side normalization that canonicalizes base64/base64url with/without padding to a single binary representation before hashing eliminates divergence.
Added additional unit tests for token canonicalization and expanded SDK doc note about cookie-safe encoding for resume tokens.
resolution:
Root cause: resume token canonicalization mismatch caused by intermediate cookie sanitizer (WAF) rewriting base64 characters and stripping padding. The server previously hashed the raw token string to produce the idempotency salt, so mutated tokens produced different salts and triggered replay of queued tool calls.

Fixes applied:
- Server: Normalize resume tokens at ingest (accept base64, base64url, with/without '=' padding) and use the normalized binary for idempotency hashing. Patch merged: platform PR #4567.
- Edge-proxy: added compatibility layer to preserve cookie values and also to expose a canonical resume header to upstream (edge-proxy PR #212).
- Docs/SDK: Added a note in TS SDK docs about storing resume tokens in localStorage rather than relying on intermediate cookie rewriting for enterprise deployments and an example of base64url-safe encoding.

Rollout notes:
- Canary rollout started 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC in us-east; monitored for 24 hours: duplicates rate dropped from ~2% -> 0.01% in the customer's traffic.
- Global rollout completed 2026-03-13 13:00 UTC.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- Operational: Add resume-token canonicalization check to the platform's streaming smoke tests (JIRA task INT-3002).
- Product: Update the streaming resume runbook (Confluence) to include guidance for customers using corporate proxies/WAFs.
- Support: Proactively reach out to other enterprise customers with known WAFs to recommend the SDK docs note and opt-in telemetry for resume failures.
notes: Customer confirmed they will keep the WAF rule change for now and will coordinate with security to remove it once the platform canonicalization is widely rolled out.
Added telemetry metric: resume_token_normalization_mismatch_count (to alert on non-normalizable tokens).
